Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by the formation of a protective glaze layer through tribo-oxidation, which is enhanced by the introduction of heterogeneous structural evolutions, such as nanocomposite/amorphous tribo-layers, precipitation-reinforced interfaces, and gradient nanograined subsurfaces.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.intervention: Introduction of heterogeneous structural evolutions, such as nanocomposite/amorphous tribo-layers, precipitation-reinforced interfaces, and gradient nanograined subsurfaces, into the FeNiCrCoCu coating
generation.structural_mediator: Tribo-oxidation and the formation of a protective glaze layer
generation.mechanism: The introduction of heterogeneous structural evolutions enhances the formation of a protective glaze layer, which reduces wear by suppressing sliding-induced deformation and promoting solid lubrication
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating at high temperatures
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu coating without heterogeneous structural evolutions
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of glaze layer formation and its relationship to the heterogeneous structural evolutions is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test at high temperatures (≥600 °C) with varying loads (10-100 N) on FeNiCrCoCu coatings with and without heterogeneous structural evolutions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate of the FeNiCrCoCu coating with heterogeneous structural evolutions is not significantly lower than that of the coating without heterogeneous structural evolutions, the hypothesis is falsified

Tribo-oxidation may promote the formation of a protective oxide layer (glaze layer) consisting of various nanocrystalline (NC) oxides on the worn surface, which assists in enhancing the friction interface while providing solid lubrication [,,]. If the worn surface is replaced by a glaze layer as tribo-oxidation accumulates, a gentle wear scenario can be achieved. Nevertheless, whether such glaze layer can be produced on the worn surface in time depends substantially on the sensitivity of the intrinsic structure in alloy matrix to tribochemical reactions. As for CCA, its wear resistance and thermal stability during high-temperature wear can be ameliorated by heterogeneous structural evolution. The intrinsic composition undulations can stabilize the friction interface and act twofold, not only by circumventing strain localization in the NC tribo-layer but also by densifying the glaze layer.
